proposedchanges.title: Trump and Other Plaintiffs Sue Social Media Companies Over Account Suspensions
proposedchanges.description_long: After social-media companies suspended Donald Trump’s accounts following the January 6 attack, Trump and other plaintiffs filed lawsuits in 2021 against major technology companies and their leaders. They alleged political censorship and sought restored account access and damages. The complaints treated the suspensions as violations of free-speech protections, but filing a lawsuit did not establish that the companies acted unlawfully. The cases renewed debate about the First Amendment’s limits on government and the separate authority private platforms use to enforce their own rules. The supplied reports document the suspensions and legal claims. They do not establish that Trump’s lawsuits forced platforms to restore his accounts, remove moderation rules, or amplify his content. Describe the censorship claims as allegations and remove assertions of a coordinated campaign or a proven constitutional violation.

evidencebasis: The packet links to Axios and BBC coverage of the January 2021 suspensions and July 2021 lawsuits. The merged medium describes the plaintiffs’ censorship allegations and requested relief. The current source URLs remain present.
notes: Replace the copied long and use neutral language for the lawsuits. Keep the legal claims attributed to plaintiffs and remove the unrelated conclusions about forced amplification and constitutional violations.
